text_blocks.snippet: Opsumit (macitentan) is a prescription medication used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). It can cause both common and serious side effects.

list.snippet: Bronchitis or upper respiratory tract infections
Severe Birth Defects: Opsumit causes major harm to an unborn baby if taken during pregnancy. Females of childbearing potential must have negative pregnancy tests and use effective contraception.

Liver Damage: It can affect liver function. Your doctor will check your liver with blood tests before you start and during treatment. Signs of liver issues include nausea, vomiting, upper right stomach pain, fatigue, loss of appetite, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin/eyes.
Fluid Retention and Edema: Swelling in the hands, legs, or feet, or rapid weight gain can happen, especially during the first weeks of treatment.
Low Red Blood Cell Levels (Anemia): Significant drops in hemoglobin can occur, sometimes requiring a blood transfusion.
Decreased Sperm Counts: Opsumit may reduce sperm counts and impact male fertility.

text_blocks.snippet: You can review full safety information on the Opsumit Official Website or check detailed drug data via GoodRx Opsumit Guide.
